extracted.intended_audience: Insured depository institutions (banks, state savings associations, insured branches of foreign banks), their senior management and counsel; FDIC supervisory staff and officials
extracted.subtask_description: FDIC's official Guidelines for Appeals of Material Supervisory Determinations describing what determinations may be appealed, who may appeal, the appellate bodies (Division Director and SARC), timelines, procedural requirements, standards of review, information-sharing, stays, and Ombudsman and anti-retaliation protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ombudsman's Role
rubrics_metrics.description: Ombudsman is a non-voting member of the SARC, will attend SARC meetings, participate in discussions, offer views/opinions/advice based on a neutral perspective, and will have access to all materials reviewed by the SARC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ombudsman will oversee sharing of information considered by the SARC, verify both parties receive materials, monitor the supervisory process after an appeal for possible retaliation, and report periodically to the Board. To avoid conflicts, the Ombudsman may designate a Regional Ombudsman or a staff member to serve where necessary (e.g., if previously involved with the institution). The Ombudsman's inclusion is intended to preserve neutrality while adding the Ombudsman's perspective to deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SARC Membership Composition and Alternates
rubrics_metrics.description: The SARC consists of three voting members (one inside FDIC Board member designated by the FDIC Chairperson serving as SARC Chairperson; plus one deputy or special assistant to each of the other inside Board members). The General Counsel and Ombudsman are non-voting members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FDIC Chairperson may designate alternates to fill vacancies provided the alternate was not involved in making or affirming the material supervisory determination under review. A SARC member may designate and authorize a member of his or her staff within the member's area of responsibility to act on his or her behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions Eligible to Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines apply to insured depository institutions the FDIC supervises (insured State nonmember banks, insured branches of foreign banks, and state savings associations) and to other insured depository institutions for which the FDIC makes material supervisory determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to institutions supervised by the FDIC or for which FDIC makes material supervisory determinations; other stakeholders are not described as appellants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinations Subject to Appeal (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution may appeal any material supervisory determination. The Guidelines list specific categories (a–q) that qualify as material supervisory determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enumerated appealable items include: (a) CAMELS ratings; (b) IT ratings under the Uniform Rating System for Information Technology; (c) Trust ratings; (d) CRA ratings; (e) Consumer compliance ratings; (f) Registered transfer agent exam ratings; (g) Government securities dealer exam ratings; (h) Municipal securities dealer exam ratings; (i) Determinations on appropriateness of loan loss reserve provisions; (j) Classifications of loans/assets in dispute exceeding 10% of total capital; (k) Determinations of violations of statutes/regulations affecting capital/earnings/operating flexibility or supervisory oversight level; (l) Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z) restitution; (m) Certain filings made under 12 CFR 303.11(f) after reconsideration; (n) Decisions to initiate informal enforcement actions (e.g., memoranda of understanding); (o) Determinations regarding compliance with a formal enforcement action (with exception noted); (p) Matters requiring board attention; and (q) Any other supervisory determination that may affect capital, earnings, operating flexibility, capital category for prompt corrective action, or supervisory oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinations Not Subject to Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain actions are excluded from appeal rights under these Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include: (a) decisions to appoint a conservator or receiver and other resolution/receivership actions (e.g., parts 370, 371, 381, §360.10); (b) decisions to take prompt corrective action under section 38 of the FDI Act; (c) determinations for which other appeals procedures exist (e.g., deposit insurance assessment risk classifications and payment calculations); and (d) formal enforcement-related actions and decisions (determinations and underlying facts forming basis of a recommended or pending formal enforcement action). Additionally, a formal enforcement-related action/decision becomes unappealable when FDIC initiates an Order of Investigation, issues a Notice of Charges or Notice of Assessment, provides a draft consent order, or otherwise provides written notice that it is reviewing for a formal enforcement action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Appeal Rights and Timeframes for Enforcement-Related Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If the FDIC provides written notice that it is determining whether a formal enforcement action is merited, specific timeframes apply before appeal rights are lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDIC must issue an Order of Investigation, Notice of Charges, or provide a draft consent order within 120 days of such notice or most recent submission of information, or appeal rights become available. If a draft consent order is provided and rejected in writing, FDIC must issue an Order of Investigation or Notice of Charges within 90 days of rejection or appeal rights become available. For referrals to Attorney General or notices to HUD under ECOA/FHA, similar timing applies. Written notification will be provided to the institution within 10 days when appeal rights become available. The relevant FDIC Division and the institution may mutually agree to extend these periods; extensions to 120/90 day periods require SARC Chairperson approval if FDIC seeks formal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-Faith Resolution Encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions should make a good-faith effort to resolve disputes concerning material supervisory determinations with the on-site examiner and/or the appropriate Regional Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-site examiner and Regional Office will promptly respond to concerns; informal resolution is encouraged but not a condition to filing a request for review with the Division or to filing a subsequent appeal with the SARC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a Request for Review with the Appropriate Division (timing and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution may file a request for review with the Division that made the determination within 60 calendar days following receipt of the report of examination or other written communication of a material supervisory determination. Requests may be submitted electronically but confidentiality is recommended (securemail.fdic.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for review must be in writing and include: (a) a detailed description of disputed issues, surrounding circumstances, institution's position and supporting arguments (including citation to statutes/regulations/policy), how resolution would materially affect the institution, and whether good-faith resolution was attempted; and (b) a statement that the institution's board of directors or senior management has considered and authorized filing (senior management defined). If senior management files an appeal, it must inform the board before filing and keep the board informed of status. The Division Director will act within 45 calendar days (see next rubric). Addresses and email for filing are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division Director Review Process and Options
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 45 calendar days after receiving a timely request for review, the Division Director will either (a) review and issue a written determination setting forth the grounds for the determination, or (b) refer the request to the SARC for appeal and provide written notice to the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing a written determination under (a), the Director will consider whether the material supervisory determination is consistent with laws, regulations, and policy, and make an independent supervisory determination without deferring to either party. The Director will inform the institution of the 30-day time period for filing with the SARC and provide the mailing address. The Division Director may request guidance from the SARC Chairperson or Legal Division on procedural questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of Division-Level Review Required Before SARC
rubrics_metrics.description: No appeal to the SARC is allowed unless the institution has first filed a timely request for review with the appropriate Division Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a jurisdictional requirement — institutions must follow the Division-level filing/timelines before proceeding to SARC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an Appeal to the SARC (timing and filing mechanics)
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution that disagrees with the Division Director's written determination may appeal to the SARC within 30 calendar days after receipt of that determination. An appeal is considered filed if received by FDIC within 30 days or if placed in U.S. mail within that 30-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals may be mailed to the address on the Division Director's determination or emailed to ESS_Appeals@fdic.gov. The FDIC will acknowledge the appeal and provide copies of the institution's appeal to the Office of the Ombudsman and the Division Director. Copies of all relevant materials related to an appeal will be provided to the Office of the Ombudsman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of an Appeal to the SARC (substance limits and evidentiary rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal should indicate it is an appeal to the SARC and include contact information, a copy of the Division Director's determination, and requests for oral presentation or expedited review if sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only matters submitted to the Division Director in the request for review may be appealed. Evidence not presented to the Division Director is generally not permitted; such evidence may be submitted to the SARC only if approved by the SARC Chairperson and allowing reasonable time for the Division Director to review/respond. The institution should set forth all legal and factual reasons it disagrees. Nothing in the process creates discovery rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof as to all matters at issue in the appeal (including timeliness) rests with the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Institution must come forward with evidence/arguments to make its case; this is distinct from the standard of review applied by the SARC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission From the Division Director to the SARC
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division Director may submit views regarding the appeal to the SARC within 30 calendar days of the date the appeal is received by the SARC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits the Division Director to present the supervisory perspective and reasoning for the original determination for SARC consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral Presentation Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The SARC will allow an oral presentation if requested by the institution or FDIC staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral presentations may be in person, telephonically, electronically, or by other mutually agreed means. If held, both the institution and FDIC staff may present positions and respond to SARC questions. Information that parties receive in time for an oral presentation must be provided timely so parties can prepare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation, Dismissal, and Rejection of Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The SARC may consolidate appeals based on similar facts for expediency. An appeal may be dismissed if not timely filed, if the basis of the appeal is not discernable, or if the institution withdraws the appeal. The SARC will decline to consider an appeal if appeal rights are not yet available under Section D(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are procedural grounds; institutions should ensure timeliness and clarity of grounds to avoid dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Review and Standard of Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The SARC is an appellate body that will make independent supervisory determinations by reviewing appeals for consistency with FDIC policies, practices, and mission and the overall reasonableness of, and support for, the positions advanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SARC review is limited to facts and circumstances as they existed prior to or at the time the material supervisory determination was made (later facts/corrective actions not considered). SARC will not consider appeals seeking to change FDIC rules or policy; appeals raising policy matters of first impression will be referred to the Chairperson's Office after consultation with Legal Division. The SARC will notify the institution in writing of its decision within 45 days after the SARC meets to consider the appeal; the SARC meeting will be held within 90 days after filing or referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of Information Considered by SARC
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials considered by the SARC will be shared with both parties to the appeal on a timely basis, subject to applicable legal limitations on disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable legal limitations include restrictions on confidential supervisory information (e.g., 12 CFR part 309) so redaction may be necessary (e.g., if materials include confidential supervisory information relating to another IDI). The Ombudsman will verify that both parties received all materials. Timing will allow the appealing institution to prepare for a meeting with the SARC if oral presentation is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Redaction of SARC Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the SARC will be published as soon as practicable and redacted to avoid disclosure of the appealing institution's name and information exempt from disclosure under FOIA and 12 CFR part 309.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If redaction is insufficient to prevent improper disclosure, published decisions may be presented in summary form. Published SARC decisions may be cited as precedent. Annual reports on SARC decisions and Division Directors' decisions will be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility, Waivers, and Supplemental Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The SARC, with concurrence of the Legal Division, retains discretion to waive any provision of the Guidelines for good cause and may adopt supplemental rules governing SARC operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may request extensions of time periods from the appropriate Division Director or the SARC Chairperson. Filings due on weekends/holidays may be made on the next business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Stay of Supervisory Action or Determination (procedure and standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions may request a stay of a supervisory action or determination from the Division Director while an appeal is pending; the request must be in writing and include reasons for the stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Division Director has discretion to grant a stay and will generally decide within 21 days of receiving the request, providing the institution written reasons for the decision. A stay may be granted subject to conditions (including time-limited conditions). The FDIC expects the stay decision may be based on factors including likelihood of irreparable or material harm. Requesting expedited SARC review may be an alternative in some circumstances. Commenters had suggested different procedures (e.g., automatic stays or SARC-decided stays), but the final Guidelines leave stay authority with Division Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination With State Regulatory Authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: When a material supervisory determination subject to review is the joint product of the FDIC and a State regulatory authority, the relevant Division Director will promptly notify the State regulatory authority and provide copies of the institution's request for review and related materials and solicit the State's views before making a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appeal is filed with the SARC, the SARC will notify both the institution and the State authority of its decision. Any remaining issues between the institution and the State regulatory authority after the SARC decision are left to those parties to resolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on Supervisory or Enforcement Actions During Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the procedures in these Guidelines does not affect, delay, or impede any formal or informal supervisory or enforcement action in progress during the appeal, nor does it affect the FDIC's authority to take supervisory or enforcement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should not expect appeals to halt ongoing supervisory/enforcement actions unless a stay is granted under the stay procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on Applications or Requests for Approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application or request for approval made to the FDIC by an institution that has appealed a material supervisory determination that relates to or could affect the approval will not be considered until a final decision concerning the appeal is made, unless the institution requests otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may elect to have the application considered before final appeal decision, but otherwise approvals are deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Examiner Retaliation and Complaint Process
rubrics_metrics.description: FDIC policy prohibits retaliation, abuse, or retribution by agency examiners or FDIC personnel against an institution that appeals. Such conduct constitutes unprofessional conduct and may result in disciplinary or remedial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ombudsman will monitor the supervision process following an appeal and report periodically to the Board. Institutions believing they have been retaliated against are encouraged to contact the Regional Director and may file a complaint with the Director, Office of the Ombudsman, explaining circumstances and requesting investigation and remedial action. The Office of the Ombudsman will work with the appropriate Division Director to resolve allegations.
